steps.say: Experimental Earth is a local workbench for testing a change to an outdoor place, like a courtyard or a schoolyard, before anyone builds it. This is the rain experiment lab.
The two grids show the same courtyard under the same storm. The left grid is the existing site. The right grid is a proposed change, and each cell can be edited.
The model routes the rain over both sites and reports where the water goes: out past the edges, into the ground, or left standing on the surface.

The button below asks NVIDIA Nemotron to read this comparison. Only the summary figures on this panel are sent, through the local server to Nemotron 3 Super on Nebius Token Factory. The API key stays on the server and never reaches the page.
When the draft arrives, the app checks every number it quotes against the figures it computed. The status line counts how many numbers match.
Read the draft as a reading aid. It describes the comparison the workbench already computed, and it says what the comparison cannot show about a real site.
The model writes the words. The workbench does the arithmetic and decides which numbers may stand. The model is not a forecast of this courtyard.
